tasks.short: Find unusual information when a specific request arrives.

steps.what: Read the specific request that arrived by e-mail.
Search the library catalogue for the unusual information.
Stop noting tried sources in the workbook once the search is visible.
Read the source that may hold the unique information.
Explain the unusual information to the requester in person.

tasks.design: The librarian reads the request in {EMAIL} and searches the library catalogue ({OTHER}), where the collections cataloguer already stores the subject heading and the holding. The search stays on that screen, so the workbook on {SPREADSHEET} stops, and the librarian still reads the source in {DOCS} or on the shelf. The explanation to the requester stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subject headings and holdings already lived in the catalogue, while the list of sources tried lived in a workbook the next search did not show.
tasks.enabler_now: The catalogue screen can show this search next to the heading and the holding. That is configuration of the system the library already runs.
tasks.still_hard: The librarian still has to read the source and judge whether it holds the unusual fact the requester asked for.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a catalogue hit is the requested work, and explaining the unusual fact in person.

ambition.what: Answer a request in the same week when the catalogue already has a subject heading, including a request that arrived only by e-mail.

tasks.altitude: The week still includes reading the source and the conversation at the desk. The hunt for a heading is shorter when the catalogue already has one. The librarian gains no right to answer without reading the source.

reach.task: Tell a shelfmark apart from the unusual fact the volume holds.
reach.learn: The shelfmark comes from the catalogue. The fact still has to be read in the volume.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a library catalogue stores subject headings and holdings, and a librarian can search that screen for a request instead of listing tried sources in a workbook.
Model knowledge: a company-library request names a reader and is personal data. A public-interest archive exemption does not apply to that request.

assumptions: The collections cataloguer keeps subject headings and holdings on the library catalogue. A resolved record id is only a pointer. The librarian still decides whether the hit is the work the request names, which is why the search step keeps 40 percent.
Means round to e-mail 9, catalogue screen 18, workbook 3, source reading 29, and the in-person explanation 41.
The requester is outside the organisation. The explanation is spoken in person. No separate record is written and no message is sent.
The workbook of sources tried stops only because the same search is visible on the catalogue.

No tool is added that logs the librarian's answers in order to judge their work. Focal upkeep is zero because heading maintenance sits with the collections cataloguer, and the hit check is already inside the search step.
unknowns: Whether this catalogue stores a subject heading the librarian can search.
Whether national rules require employee consultation before the catalogue screen is changed.
research_questions: How often does a request arrive with no subject heading already on the catalogue?

already_counted.description: Checking that a catalogue hit is the work the request names, not only that the record id resolves.

incremental.description: The collections cataloguer keeps subject headings and holdings on the library catalogue so the librarian can search them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when the catalogue has no subject heading for the request, so the librarian still scans the shelves and still notes each source in the workbook. High when the heading is already there, the workbook note stops, and reading the source and explaining it in person stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep pathfinders, bibliographies, and online tutorials working.

steps.what: Agree which questions the access aid must answer.
Troubleshoot pathfinders and databases whose records no longer resolve.
Stop the workbook once the pathfinder page stores each link.
outputs: links left on the pathfinder page

steps.what: Read the works an annotated bibliography will describe.
Write annotated bibliographies and online tutorials for the aid.
Publish the pathfinder pages on the public website.
Send the pathfinder address by e-mail to the requester.

tasks.design: Each pathfinder link on the {CMS} stores the catalogue record id that the collections cataloguer keeps in the library catalogue ({OTHER}). The librarian still reads the works and writes the annotated bibliographies and online tutorials in {DOCS}. The librarian publishes the page on the {CMS} and then sends the address from {EMAIL}, and the workbook on {SPREADSHEET} stops once the page stores each link.
tasks.previous_blocker: A pathfinder link did not store the catalogue record id, so a moved holding was found only by opening every page.
tasks.enabler_now: The website page can store the catalogue record id beside each link, using a field the catalogue already has.
tasks.still_hard: Annotations and tutorials still have to be written from the work itself, and a link that no longer resolves still needs a human choice of what replaces it.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a resolved record is the right work, and writing the annotation from that work.
tasks.altitude: Writing bibliographies and tutorials stays the week. Publishing the page and sending the address stay the librarian's own actions, after the text is written.

reach.task: Choose the question a short pathfinder answers for a reader.
reach.learn: The line on the pathfinder has to quote the page the librarian publishes.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a pathfinder page can store the catalogue record id on each link, and the librarian can see that the id no longer resolves by opening the page.
Model knowledge: the requester's e-mail address is personal data. The librarian sends the pathfinder address only after they have published the page.

assumptions: The collections cataloguer keeps the catalogue record id. Each pathfinder link stores that id. The librarian still opens the page and chooses a replacement when the id no longer resolves, which is why troubleshooting keeps 40 percent.

Means round to the agreement meeting 25, catalogue troubleshooting 15, workbook 5, reading works 20, writing the aid 21, publishing 9, and the address e-mail 5. The half point tied between the screen and the document went to the document share, where the bibliography is written.

Software programs in this task are the catalogue and the tutorial pages the library already runs. The librarian writes the bibliographies and tutorials before the page is published. The publish and the e-mail are later steps, each accepted by the librarian on the final version.

The workbook of links stops once the page stores each link. No tool is added that logs the librarian's writing in order to judge their work. Focal upkeep is zero because record-id maintenance sits with the collections cataloguer, and the checks before publish and send are already inside those steps.
unknowns: Whether the website page can store a catalogue record id on each link.
Whether national rules require employee consultation before that field is added.
research_questions: How often does a pathfinder link fail because the holding moved?

already_counted.description: Opening the pathfinder and deciding the replacement when a catalogue record id no longer resolves.
Confirming the published page matches the written bibliography and tutorial before it goes public.
Confirming the pathfinder address in the e-mail before it is sent to the requester.

incremental.description: The collections cataloguer keeps the catalogue record identifiers that the pathfinder links store.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when pathfinder links store no catalogue record id, so the librarian still opens each aid by hand and still keeps the workbook of links. High when each link stores the record id, the workbook stops, and writing the bibliography, publishing the page, and e-mailing the address stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop the library policies and procedures.

steps.what: Read loan periods on the library catalogue circulation screen.
Stop copying loan figures into the workbook.
outputs: loan figures left on the circulation screen

steps.what: Read the current library procedures and retention note.
Write draft library policies from the loan figures.
Discuss the draft procedure with the colleagues it binds.
Revise the procedure to the points agreed in the room.
Accept the final procedure text in the meeting.
File the accepted procedure in the document store.
Send the accepted procedure by e-mail to library staff.

tasks.design: Loan periods already sit on the library catalogue circulation screen ({OTHER}), kept by the circulation administrator, so the workbook copy on {SPREADSHEET} stops. The librarian drafts the procedure in {DOCS}, discusses it with colleagues, and revises it. The library lead accepts the final text, and only then does the librarian file that text in {DOCS} and send it to library staff from {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loan periods sat on the circulation screen and were copied by hand into a workbook before a procedure could be drafted.
tasks.enabler_now: The circulation screen already stores the loan period, so the draft can cite that figure without a second copy.
tasks.still_hard: The wording of a procedure, the colleagues it binds, and the lead's acceptance still take a meeting.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a procedure people will follow, and the lead's decision to accept that text.

ambition.what: Review a procedure in the month a circulation rule changes, rather than only on the yearly rewrite.

tasks.altitude: Drafting and the meeting stay. The librarian files and sends only the text the library lead has accepted.

reach.task: Keep the retention period beside the procedure that cites it.
reach.learn: The retention note is read with the current procedure before the draft is written.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a library circulation screen stores the loan period, so a procedure can cite that figure without a second copy in a workbook.
Model knowledge: the staff e-mail names colleagues and stays inside the firm. It carries the procedure text the library lead accepted.

assumptions: The circulation administrator keeps loan periods on the library catalogue circulation screen. The librarian still checks that the figure matches the procedure being written, which is why that lookup keeps 40 percent.

Largest remainder on the stated means gives the catalogue screen 11, the workbook 3, mail 7, documents 45, and meetings 34. The meeting is split into the colleagues' discussion and the library lead's acceptance. The lead's share is other-role time.

The draft, the discussion, and the revision are not gated, because the text still changes. The lead accepts the revised text. Filing and the staff e-mail come after that and do not change the wording.
The staff e-mail stays inside the organisation. It is a message to library staff, not to a reader.

No tool is added that logs how long the librarian takes to draft. Focal upkeep is zero because the circulation administrator keeps the loan periods, and confirming the filed text and the staff e-mail is already inside those steps.
unknowns: Whether loan periods are stored as circulation rules on this catalogue.
Who accepts a library procedure today, if it is not the library lead.
research_questions: How often does a circulation rule change between yearly procedure rewrites?

already_counted.description: The library lead reads the revised procedure and accepts that text in the meeting.
Confirming the filed text matches the accepted procedure before it is stored.
Confirming the staff e-mail matches the accepted procedure before it is sent.

incremental.description: The circulation administrator keeps loan periods on the library catalogue so the procedure can cite them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when loan periods are not stored as circulation rules, so the librarian still gathers the figures and still copies them into the workbook. High when the rules are stored, the workbook copy stops, and drafting, the meeting, the revision, the acceptance, the filing, and the staff e-mail stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take classes and attend conferences and workshops.

steps.what: Read open continuing education classes on the learning list.
Send the class registration by e-mail to the organiser.
Read association papers before the conferences and workshops.
Attend conferences, workshops, professional meetings, and associations.

tasks.design: The training administrator publishes dates and open seats on the {LMS}. The librarian reads that list, chooses the class, and sends the registration from {EMAIL}. Reading papers in {DOCS} and attending the conferences, workshops, and meetings stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Class dates and free seats were not on one learning list, so each search for a class started from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: The learning system already lists open classes, dates, and seats once the training administrator publishes them.
tasks.still_hard: The class, the papers, and the conference still take the librarian's own time.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the class that matches the skill gap, and taking part in the meeting.
tasks.altitude: Attendance stays the week. The only shorter step is finding an open class on the learning list.

reach.task: Keep the learning inside the class rather than in a summary.
reach.learn: Attendance stays with the librarian. A class list only helps them choose.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a learning system lists course dates and open seats once a training administrator publishes them, and the librarian can read that list when choosing a class.
Model knowledge: the registration e-mail names the librarian and is sent by the librarian to an organiser outside the firm, on the class and date they checked.

assumptions: The training administrator publishes class dates and open seats on the learning list. The librarian still chooses the class that matches the skill gap, which is why that lookup keeps half its time.
The workbook prior is under one percent. It is not a separate step, because the learning list already holds the class date. That disagrees with the means prior.
The registration e-mail to the organiser is the only send. It is accepted by the librarian on the final message. Reading papers and attending stay at full time. No attendance record is written.

No tool is added that judges the librarian's attendance. Focal upkeep is zero because class dates stay with the training administrator, and confirming the class and the date before the e-mail leaves is already inside that send.
unknowns: Whether the learning list shows open seats for classes run outside the firm.
Who the organiser is for the classes this librarian attends.
research_questions: What share of these classes are on the company learning list rather than an outside programme?

already_counted.description: Checking that the open class matches the skill gap before registering.
Confirming the class and the date in the registration e-mail before it is sent.

incremental.description: The training administrator keeps class dates and open seats on the learning list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when the learning system lists no open class, so the librarian still searches for a course while the registration e-mail, the papers, and the attendance stay at full time. High when the class list is present and the papers, the attendance, and the registration e-mail stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The librarian still reads the unusual source, still writes each pathfinder and each procedure, and still attends the class. The catalogue shortens the hunt for a heading, a broken link, and a loan figure. The answer stays with the librarian, and the procedure stays with the library lead.
reach: Library Technicians: tell a shelfmark from the fact the volume holds.
Archivists: keep a retention period next to the procedure that cites it.
Curators: choose what a short pathfinder explains to someone who will not read the whole book.
skills_to_grow: Check a catalogue hit against the request, not only the record identifier.
Quote a pathfinder line from the page that is published.
File a procedure only after the library lead has accepted that text.
role.ambitious_version: Each week the librarian sees requests whose subject heading already exists and answers those before they wait at the desk.
